description: MK import charges (customs duty, motor-vehicle tax, import VAT) and landed cost per car, fixed EUR 700 transport, whole units. price = real purchase price (landed cost, profit); estimated_customs_value_eur + source (e.g. SchwackeNet) = primary charges' basis; transaction_value = on price paid; recorded listing values apply. indicative_preview = rules that are not ACTIVE (draft, under review or approved but not yet activated; see rule.status): relay banner unchanged. Missing CO2 document or proof of origin changes the result; unknown charges are never 0. Read-only; no tool approves tax rules.

errorSchema.description: Typed tool error (``isError: true`` result content). Same codes as the dashboard API.
errorSchema.title: ToolError

inputSchema.description: A listing, vehicle facts or both; every vehicle field that is set replaces the listing's.

accept_previous_month_fx.description: Indicative preview only: accept last month's recorded customs rate (labelled).

customs_eur_mkd_rate.description: 1 EUR = this many MKD on the Customs monthly list of the declaration month. Used only when no customs rate is recorded for that month; labelled and never stored.

listing_id.description: Listing whose CURRENT revision supplies the facts: advertised price, fuel, CO2 claim, first registration, Euro class, seller country, mileage. The owner's RECORDED values of the listing are used automatically: the real purchase price instead of the advertised one and the estimated customs value (fact source recorded). Omit to estimate from vehicle alone.

vehicle.description: Facts you know (better): each field set here replaces the listing's.

co2.description: CO2 figures as printed, at most one per cycle; an empty list clears the listing's claim.

items.description: One CO2 figure exactly as printed on the document, with its measurement cycle.

cycle.description: Cycle printed next to the figure. WLTP is used when present, otherwise NEDC; nedc_correlated and unknown leave the CO2 charge unknown (never converted).

co2_document.description: Where the CO2 figure is printed: coc, registration_consent, manufacturer_certificate or technical_assessment_certificate; listing_claim_unverified for an advertised figure; none_available ONLY when no document exists (the rules then apply their deemed charge). Unknown leaves the motor-vehicle tax unknown.

co2_round_up_confirmed.description: true: a non-integer CO2 figure may be rounded up (labelled assumption); otherwise it stays unknown.

declaration_date.description: Customs declaration date (YYYY-MM-DD); default today. Selects the rules and the monthly customs rate.

emissions_class.description: Euro class as stated, e.g. "Euro 5" (the import gate only; it never changes an amount).

estimated_customs_value_eur.description: ESTIMATED customs value of the vehicle in EUR, without transport (e.g. the SchwackeNet catalogue value Customs uses for used vehicles; more than 0). The primary scenario's charges use it + the transport to the MK place of entry; the landed cost and the profit still use price. Adds the transaction_value scenario (Customs accepts the price paid, its primary method). Omitted with listing_id: the owner's recorded estimate of the listing, if any. Needs estimated_customs_value_source.

estimated_customs_value_source.description: Where the estimated customs value comes from, e.g. "SchwackeNet catalogue" or "owner estimate" (3-120 characters); only with estimated_customs_value_eur.

first_registration.description: First registration as YYYY, YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD (never completed with invented parts).

fuel.description: Fuel or drive type; unknown leaves the CO2 charge unknown.

hs_code.description: Tariff code from a broker, ruling or owner statement (HS 8703 only; never inferred). A plug-in hybrid needs it.

importer_status.description: private, non_vat_business or vat_dealer (VAT recoverability note only).

mileage_km.description: Odometer reading in km (used or new).

origin_proof.description: Proof of preferential origin held; omitted means no proof (standard duty).

country.description: Origin country stated on the proof (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, or EU); required for efta and cefta.

kind.description: none: no proof, so standard duty (the default); unknown: the duty stays unknown; eu, efta, tr, uk, cefta, ua, us: a held proof, assumed accepted by Customs, with the standard-duty alternative shown next to it.

price.description: REAL purchase price (what is, or will be, actually paid): the landed cost and the profit always use it, never the estimated customs value. Omitted with listing_id: the owner's recorded purchase price of the listing when there is one (fact source recorded), otherwise its advertised price. Set price_basis invoice for an invoice or contract price; otherwise it counts as an advertised price (a claim, flagged).

currency.description: EUR or MKD. A CHF price leaves the customs value unknown (two customs rates would be needed; a reference rate is never substituted).

price_basis.description: invoice (transaction value) or advertised (the default for a price passed here). Without a price it restates the listing's advertised price; it is refused when the listing has a recorded purchase price (that keeps its recorded kind: pass a price to replace it).

seller_country.description: Seller country (recorded; never implies the origin).

transport_after_entry_eur.description: Inland leg after the MK place of entry, only when it is separately invoiced (then also set transport_after_entry_separately_invoiced true): it leaves the customs value and enters the import VAT base alone.

items.description:
One labelled scenario (``primary`` first). In ``active`` mode the totals are ``total``,
``total_eur`` and ``landed_cost_eur`` (the ``indicative_*`` fields are null); in a preview
the reverse. A total is known only when the calculation is complete; otherwise it is
unknown and ``known_subtotal`` (labelled, never a total) shows what resolved. The landed cost
is the REAL purchase price + transport + this scenario's charges; ``customs_value_kind`` says
whether the charges rest on the estimated customs value or the transaction value.
``customs_value`` is the engine input in its own currency (EUR, or MKD for an MKD price);
``customs_value_eur`` is the same value in whole euros at the customs rate, so the scenarios
compare in one currency.
